faq.q: What parts are usually labeled on a black hole diagram?
faq.a: There is no single official four-part list. Student diagrams commonly label the event horizon, black-hole shadow, accretion disk, and central singularity; more detailed diagrams may also show the photon sphere or photon rings, corona, and jets.

faq.q: Does a black hole suck in everything like a vacuum cleaner?
faq.a: No. Far from the event horizon, a black hole's gravity behaves like the gravity of any other object with the same mass. Objects can orbit a black hole without falling in.

faq.q: What did the Event Horizon Telescope image?
faq.a: The Event Horizon Telescope reconstructed radio images of hot emission around M87* and Sagittarius A*, revealing a bright ring surrounding a central dark shadow consistent with general relativity. It did not directly photograph a physical event-horizon surface or a singularity.
